claims.text: BARTScore outperforms existing top-scoring metrics in 16 of 22 test settings across 16 datasets and 7 evaluation perspectives.
Adding the prompt 'such as' to translated text when using BARTScore leads to a 3 percentage point absolute improvement in Kendall's Tau correlation on German-English machine translation evaluation.
BARTScore conceptualizes generated text evaluation as a sequence-to-sequence text generation problem modeled using pre-trained language models.
Fine-tuning BART on summarization and paraphrase datasets increases BARTScore's average Kendall's Tau correlation across WMT19 machine translation language pairs to 0.331.
BARTScore fine-tuned on CNNDM achieves an accuracy of 0.836 on the Rank19 factuality benchmark and a Pearson correlation of 0.735 on QAGS-CNN.

evidence.description: It can outperform existing top-scoring metrics in 16 of 22 test settings, covering evaluation of 16 datasets (e.g., machine translation, text summarization) and 7 different perspectives (e.g., informativeness, factuality).

For example, simply adding the phrase 'such as ' to the translated text when using BARTScore can lead to a 3% point absolute improvement in correlation on 'German-English' machine translation (MT) evaluation.
In this work, we conceptualize the evaluation of generated text as a text generation problem, modeled using pre-trained sequence-to-sequence models.
+ CNN + Para achieves 0.331 average Kendall's Tau correlation across all language pairs on WMT19.
BARTScore + CNN achieves 0.836 Accuracy on Rank19 and 0.735 Pearson correlation on QAGS-CNN.

methodologies.name: BARTScore
methodologies.description: An unsupervised evaluation metric that formulates text generation evaluation as conditional generation log probability under pre-trained encoder-decoder sequence-to-sequence models like BART.

limitations.text: BARTScore is less effective at distinguishing the quality of extractive summarization systems compared to abstractive summarization systems.
Combining prompt ensembling with BARTScore does not produce consistent evaluation performance improvements for factuality and linguistic quality perspectives.
Existing feature-extraction metrics like BERTScore and MoverScore do not utilize the output prediction layer of pre-trained models, leading to potential under-utilization of parameters.

PRISM formulates evaluation strictly as a paraphrasing task requiring identical semantic meaning, limiting its application to scenarios like summarization factuality evaluation where source and summary differ in semantic space.

future_work.text: Explore how to better design and utilize prompts for factuality and linguistic quality evaluation scenarios.
Develop co-evolving evaluation metrics and generation systems where improved generation systems directly serve as automated evaluation metrics.
